name: Aribwatsa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Read Holzknecht 1997 'Aribwatsa: a lost language of the Markham Family' (PL D-89, ANU repository; zero 'stress' hits) and Holzknecht 1989 PL C-115 Aribwatsa section (Table 4.15): no stress description.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1997. Aribwatsa: a 'lost' language of the Markham Family, Papua New Guinea? In S.A. Wurm (ed.), Materials on languages in danger of disappearing in the Asia-Pacific region No. 1: Some endangered languages of Papua New Guinea: Kaki Ae, Musom, and Aribwatsa, 145-163. Pacific Linguistics D-89. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-D89.145.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number P40.5.L33 M384 1997); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number P40.5.L33 M384 1997
sources.note: Sec. 2.1 Phonology (pp. 153-154) consists only of Table 2 consonants (with free alternations), Table 3 vowels and Table 4 POC reflexes across Lower Markham; no sentence on stress, accent, tone, prosody or syllable structure anywhere in the 19-page paper (zero a full-text search for stress/accent hits). Author warns (pp. 146-147) that the single 80-year-old rememberer's 'pronunciation was certainly inconsistent'.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1997. Aribwatsa word list. In Wurm (ed.), PL D-89, 164-182. DOI 10.15144/PL-D89.164.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Thematic wordlist from Butoawe (Aug 1985), practical orthography (apostrophe = glottal stop); no stress marks, no note on stress.

sources.note: For Musom only: 'Vowels in a final syllable may be dropped, or centralised, if the word has more than one syllable. The vowel in the unstressed syllable becomes schwa', e.g. 'apun > ['apm]; no rule stated and nothing said about Aribwatsa.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C115. (Glottolog ref 158598)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.note: Sec. 4.2.14 Aribwatsa, p. 59: Table 4.15 phonemes plus three allophony notes (oral~nasal voiced stops, b~beta, f~h); no stress statement. In the whole book 'stress' occurs only in a dialect-perception remark, Duwet note 11 (unstressed vowel sequences) and a Watut historical 'through stress rules' remark; no stress rule for any Markham language.
